series: Walkthrough for the bank Short craft-fair-booth-315.json, built Oct 7, 2026 for CMO review
hook: A $150 booth fee is really $315.60 for the day
hook_say: This video shows what a $150 craft fair booth really costs for the day, and how many pieces you need to sell to cover it.

rows.label: Booth fee
rows.why: Start with the booth fee, the number every maker sees first. The example show charges $150 for a 7-hour selling day.

rows.label: Miles, meals, extras, display
rows.why: Then the costs that ride along with it: 60 miles at 76 cents, organizer extras, parking, meals, and $50 as this show's share of a $300 display. Together, $165.60.

rows.label: What the day really costs
rows.why: So the day really costs $315.60. The booth fee is only 48% of it, which is why pricing against the booth fee alone sets your target too low.

rows.label: Each piece clears
rows.why: Next, what one sale leaves you. Across the five example products, an average piece sells for $13.84 and clears $6.24 after materials, making time at $20 an hour, packaging and the card fee.

rows.label: Pieces to break even
rows.why: Divide the day's cost by what each piece clears and you get 51 pieces, or $705.84 in sales, before the show earns anything. That is about 7.3 pieces every selling hour.

rows.label: Soy candle price
rows.why: The price check flags the soy candle. At $22 it sits below materials plus labor doubled, which is $23. Raise it to $26.

fix.label: Pieces to break even now
fix.why: Same show, same costs, one price change: the break-even drops from 51 pieces to 44. Run this before you pay for the booth, not after.

A $150 booth fee turns into $315.60 once miles, meals, extras and a share of your display are counted. At $6.24 cleared per piece, that is 51 pieces before the show earns anything, and raising the candle from $22 to $26 brings it to 44. Example numbers from the Craft Fair Profit Calculator; yours go in the yellow cells.
